title: Hotel Booking System
description: Design a hotel booking system where users search, book, and manage hotel room reservations with real-time availability.
functionalRequirements: Search hotels by location, dates, and guest count
View room types, amenities, photos, and pricing
Book one or more rooms for a date range
Modify or cancel existing bookings
Support room type pricing rules (weekends, seasonal)
Process payments and issue booking confirmations
Hotel admins can manage rooms, prices, and availability
nonFunctionalRequirements: Handle 10,000 concurrent search requests with sub-second response
Prevent double-booking of the same room via ACID transactions
Payment processing with exactly-once semantics
Availability data can be slightly stale (eventual consistency acceptable for search, strong for booking)
hints: Core entities: Hotel, Room, RoomType, Booking, Guest, Payment, PricingRule. Room has a RoomType (standard, deluxe, suite) and a BookingCalendar tracking reserved dates.

For availability search, use an interval-based approach: query rooms where no existing Booking overlaps [checkIn, checkOut). For concurrency safety, use optimistic locking or a distributed lock when finalizing a booking.
Use the Strategy pattern for pricing: BasePriceStrategy, WeekendSurchargeStrategy, SeasonalStrategy can be chained using the Decorator pattern. The final price = base × all applicable modifiers.

title: Movie Ticket Booking
description: Design a system like BookMyShow — users can browse movies, select showtimes, pick seats, and book tickets.
functionalRequirements: Browse movies currently showing in theatres near the user
View available showtimes for a movie
Select seats from an interactive seat map
Reserve seats for 10 minutes while payment is processed
Book tickets and receive a confirmation with QR code
Support cancellation with refund policy
Theatre admins manage movies and showtimes
nonFunctionalRequirements: Seat reservation must be atomic — two users cannot book the same seat
System handles flash booking spikes (e.g., popular movie release)
Seat map must reflect real-time availability
Temporary reservation expires automatically after 10 minutes
hints: Core entities: Movie, Theatre, Screen, Show, Seat, Booking, Payment, User. Each Show links a Movie to a Screen at a specific time. Seat has a status (Available, Temporarily Reserved, Booked) and position (row, column).

For seat reservation, use a two-phase approach: phase 1 = temporarily lock the seat with a TTL (10 min) using a distributed lock or a database reservation record; phase 2 = confirm and charge payment, then mark as Booked.

Model seats with SeatType (Regular, Premium, VIP) that affects pricing. Use the Observer pattern to notify waiting users when a reserved seat is released. The Show's seat map can be modeled as a 2D boolean array for quick availability display.

title: Food Delivery App
description: Design a food delivery platform like Zomato or Swiggy — users order food from restaurants and get real-time delivery tracking.
functionalRequirements: Users browse restaurants filtered by cuisine, rating, and delivery time
Add items to cart and place orders
Real-time order status: placed → accepted → preparing → picked up → delivered
Delivery agent assigned automatically based on proximity
Live tracking of delivery agent on a map
Rating and review system for restaurants and agents
Support multiple payment methods and promo codes
nonFunctionalRequirements: Delivery agent assignment within 30 seconds of order placement
Location updates pushed every 5 seconds during delivery
System handles 100,000 active orders concurrently
Order status updates delivered with < 2 second latency
hints: Core entities: User, Restaurant, MenuItem, Order, OrderItem, DeliveryAgent, DeliveryAssignment, Payment, Review. Order has a state machine: Placed → Accepted → Preparing → ReadyForPickup → PickedUp → Delivered.

For agent assignment, use a geospatial query to find available agents within a radius. Score them by distance + current load. Use a pub/sub system (e.g., message queue) to notify the best agent — if they decline, try the next.
Use the Observer pattern for real-time updates: Order is the subject; User, Restaurant, DeliveryAgent are observers. When order status changes, push updates to all subscribers via WebSocket.

title: Amazon Locker System
description: Design Amazon\
functionalRequirements: Assign an available locker of appropriate size for a package
Notify the customer with a one-time access code when package is stored
Customer enters code to unlock and retrieve package
Handle packages not picked up within the return window (3 days)
Multiple locker locations — find the nearest to delivery address
Locker sizes: small, medium, large, extra-large
nonFunctionalRequirements: Code verification must be instant (< 100ms)
One-time codes expire after 72 hours
System handles 500 lockers per location with concurrent access
Audit log of all access events
hints: Core entities: LockerLocation, Locker, LockerSize, Package, AccessCode, Notification. LockerLocation has many Lockers; each Locker tracks its size, availability, and current package.

For locker assignment, match the package's size to the smallest available locker that fits it. Generate a cryptographically random 6-digit AccessCode with an expiry timestamp. Store the code hashed in the DB.

Model the package lifecycle as a State Machine: InTransit → StoredInLocker → Retrieved / ReturnInitiated → ReturnedToWarehouse. When the 72-hour window expires, a background job changes state to ReturnInitiated.

title: Splitwise / Expense Splitter
description: Design an expense splitting app where groups of users can track shared expenses, split costs, and settle debts.
functionalRequirements: Users create groups (trips, households, friends)
Add expenses and split them equally, unequally, by percentage, or by shares
Show each member's net balance (how much they owe or are owed)
Simplify debts: minimize the number of transactions needed to settle
Record settlements when someone pays back
Multi-currency support with exchange rates
Expense history and detailed breakdown
nonFunctionalRequirements: Balance calculation is always consistent (no rounding errors)
Debt simplification runs in O(n log n)
Support groups up to 50 members
All monetary amounts stored as integers (cents) to avoid floating-point issues
hints: Core entities: User, Group, Expense, ExpenseSplit, Settlement. An Expense has a payer and multiple Splits (each split records who owes what amount). Balance = sum(what others owe me) − sum(what I owe others).
For split types, use the Strategy pattern: EqualSplit, PercentageSplit, ExactSplit, ShareSplit — each implements calculateAmounts(totalAmount, members). This makes adding new split types easy.

Debt simplification uses a greedy algorithm: compute each person's net balance. Keep two heaps (max-creditors and max-debtors). Each step: take the biggest creditor and biggest debtor, settle the smaller amount, repeat. This minimizes transactions.

title: Cab Booking System
description: Design a ride-hailing platform like Uber (simplified) — users request rides, drivers accept, and the system manages matching and pricing.
functionalRequirements: Rider requests a ride specifying pickup and drop-off locations
System matches the rider to the nearest available driver
Show estimated fare before confirming the ride
Driver can accept or reject the ride request
Real-time trip tracking for both rider and driver
Fare calculation based on distance, time, and surge pricing
Rating system for riders and drivers
nonFunctionalRequirements: Driver matching completes within 5 seconds of request
Support 1 million active rides concurrently
Location updates every 3 seconds during a trip
Surge pricing calculated in real-time based on supply/demand
hints: Core entities: Rider, Driver, Vehicle, Trip, TripRequest, Location, FareCalculator, Rating. Trip has a State Machine: Requested → DriverAccepted → InProgress → Completed / Cancelled.

For driver matching, maintain drivers in a geospatial index (e.g., QuadTree or geohash grid). Query for available drivers within radius R, rank by distance, and send requests sequentially until one accepts or R expands.

Surge pricing uses a multiplier based on demand/supply ratio in a geographic zone. FareCalculator applies: base_fare + (distance × per_km_rate + time × per_min_rate) × surge_multiplier. Use the Strategy pattern for different vehicle types (economy, premium, XL).

title: Online Shopping Cart
description: Design an e-commerce shopping cart system supporting product catalogue, cart management, promotions, checkout, and order tracking.
functionalRequirements: Browse and search the product catalog with filters
Add, update, or remove items from the cart
Apply promo codes and automatic discounts
Checkout with address selection and payment
Inventory management — prevent overselling
Order history with status tracking
Wishlist to save items for later
nonFunctionalRequirements: Cart operations must be atomic to prevent inventory inconsistency
Search results returned within 300ms
Flash sale: handle 50,000 concurrent purchases of the same product
Cart data persisted across sessions and devices
hints: Core entities: Product, Inventory, Cart, CartItem, Order, OrderItem, Payment, Address, Coupon, User. Cart is user-scoped and can exist before checkout. Order is created from Cart on checkout.

Use optimistic locking for inventory: read stock count, decrement in the same transaction with a WHERE stock >= requested_qty. If 0 rows affected, reject the order. This prevents overselling without full table locks.

For promotions, use the Chain of Responsibility or Composite pattern: DiscountRule interface with evaluate(cart) → discount. Chain: ProductDiscount → CategoryDiscount → CouponDiscount → BulkDiscount. Apply all and sum (or take the best).

title: Online Stock Brokerage
description: Design an online stock trading system where users place buy/sell orders that are matched through an order book.
functionalRequirements: Users place market orders and limit orders to buy or sell stocks
Order book matches buy and sell orders by price-time priority
Real-time price updates as orders are matched
Cancel an unmatched pending order
Portfolio view: current holdings and P&L
Order history and trade confirmations
Support stop-loss and take-profit orders
nonFunctionalRequirements: Order matching completes in < 1ms
Handle 100,000 orders per second
Order book operations O(log n) using sorted data structures
All matched trades stored durably with exactly-once semantics
hints: Core entities: Order, OrderType (Market/Limit/StopLoss), Side (Buy/Sell), OrderBook, Trade, Portfolio, Stock, MatchingEngine. Each stock has its own OrderBook with two sorted lists: asks (ascending price) and bids (descending price).

For matching: when a buy limit order arrives, compare with the lowest ask. If ask_price ≤ buy_price, match them (create a Trade), reduce quantities, and remove filled orders. Use a PriorityQueue (min-heap for asks, max-heap for bids).

For market orders: match immediately at the best available price regardless of limit. For partial fills: when a new order quantity > available at best price, fill what's available, then continue down the order book until fully filled or book is exhausted.

title: Car Rental System
description: Design a car rental platform like Hertz or Avis — users search available cars, book them, and manage reservations.
functionalRequirements: Browse available cars by type, location, and date range
Reserve a car for a date range with pickup/drop location
Multiple car categories: economy, sedan, SUV, luxury, electric
Dynamic pricing by category, duration, and season
Extend, modify, or cancel reservations
Track vehicle location and mileage
Late return fees and damage report on return
nonFunctionalRequirements: Prevent double-booking of the same vehicle
Search returns available cars within 200ms
Support 1,000 locations and 100,000 vehicles
hints: Core entities: Vehicle, VehicleCategory, Location, Reservation, Payment, Customer, RentalBranch. Vehicle tracks its status (Available, Reserved, Rented, Maintenance) and has a ReservationCalendar of blocked date ranges.

For availability search, query vehicles at the requested location whose status is Available and have no Reservation overlapping [startDate, endDate). Use an interval tree or indexed date-range query for efficiency.
Use the Strategy pattern for pricing: BaseDailyRate × CategoryMultiplier × SeasonalMultiplier × DurationDiscount. The Factory pattern for creating different VehicleCategory pricing strategies.

title: Flight Reservation System
description: Design a flight reservation system like MakeMyTrip — users search flights, book seats, and manage itineraries.
functionalRequirements: Search flights by origin, destination, date, and passenger count
View flight details: airline, duration, stops, price
Select specific seats from a seat map
Book single or round-trip flights with passenger details
Generate e-ticket with PNR code
Cancel booking with refund based on policy
Support multiple fare classes: economy, business, first
nonFunctionalRequirements: Seat booking is atomic — prevent double-booking
Search across 10,000 flights returns in < 500ms
PNR generation is globally unique
hints: Core entities: Airport, Flight, Aircraft, Seat, FlightInstance (a specific date's occurrence), Booking, Passenger, Ticket, FareClass. FlightInstance has a SeatMap — each Seat has a status (Available, Locked, Booked) and a FareClass.

For booking, use a two-phase lock: phase 1 = temporarily lock selected seats (TTL 10 min) while payment is processed; phase 2 = confirm booking on successful payment. Use optimistic locking on the Seat status field.

PNR = 6-character alphanumeric code (A-Z, 0-9). Generate using a combination of random bytes + checksum. Store in a hash map for O(1) lookup. Use the Facade pattern for the booking flow: SearchFacade, ReservationFacade, PaymentFacade.

title: Stack Overflow / Q&A Platform
description: Design a developer Q&A platform like Stack Overflow with questions, answers, votes, tags, reputation, and search.
functionalRequirements: Users post questions with a title, body, and tags
Other users post answers to questions
Upvote and downvote questions and answers
Accept the best answer (only by question owner)
Reputation system: gains/loses points based on votes
Tag-based browsing and search by title/body
Comments on questions and answers
Badges awarded for reputation milestones and achievements
nonFunctionalRequirements: Search returns results in < 200ms
Reputation updates are eventually consistent
Support 10 million questions and 50 million answers
hints: Core entities: User, Question, Answer, Comment, Tag, Vote, Reputation, Badge. Question and Answer both extend a Post abstract class with common fields: body, createdAt, author, voteCount, comments.

For voting, use a Vote entity linking (voter, post, value: +1/-1) with a unique constraint to prevent double-voting. Reputation change: question upvote = +10, answer upvote = +10, downvote = -2, accepted answer = +15.

For search, build a full-text inverted index: Map<word, List<postId>>. Tag filtering uses a TagIndex: Map<tag, List<questionId>>. Combine results with AND/OR logic and rank by (voteCount × 0.6 + recency × 0.4).

title: LinkedIn / Professional Network
description: Design a professional networking platform like LinkedIn — profiles, connections, feed, job postings, and messaging.
functionalRequirements: User profiles with experience, education, skills, and endorsements
Send and accept connection requests (1st/2nd/3rd degree)
News feed showing posts and activity from connections
Job postings: companies post jobs, users apply
Skill endorsements and recommendations
Direct messaging between connected users
People You May Know suggestions
nonFunctionalRequirements: Connection graph traversal for 2nd-degree connections in < 500ms
Feed loads in < 300ms for users with up to 5,000 connections
People You May Know computed offline and cached
hints: Core entities: User, Profile, Connection, Post, Job, Application, Endorsement, Recommendation, Message. The connection graph is an undirected graph — store edges as (userId1, userId2, status: Pending/Connected).

For People You May Know: compute mutual connection count for 2nd-degree connections (BFS depth 2 from user). Rank by mutual_count. Run offline nightly and cache per user. Use a graph DB or adjacency list representation.

Feed uses fan-out on write for users with < 5,000 connections: push post to all connections' feed caches on create. For power users (> 5,000), fan-out on read: merge their posts at query time with the pre-built feed.

title: Music Streaming (Spotify)
description: Design a music streaming service like Spotify — song catalog, playlists, playback queues, recommendations, and offline mode.
functionalRequirements: Browse and search songs, albums, artists, and podcasts
Create, edit, and share playlists
Play songs with skip, repeat, shuffle controls
Like songs and follow artists and playlists
Personalized daily mixes and discover weekly
Download songs for offline playback (premium)
Real-time lyrics display
Collaborative playlists (multiple editors)
nonFunctionalRequirements: Song start latency < 500ms globally via CDN
Support 400 million users, 80 million songs
Offline playback works without network
Recommendation model updated daily
hints: Core entities: User, Song, Album, Artist, Playlist, PlaybackQueue, Like, Download, ListeningHistory. Song metadata (title, duration, artist) stored in a relational DB; audio files stored in object storage distributed via CDN.

Playback queue is a user-session data structure: ordered list of song IDs with a currentIndex. Shuffle uses Fisher-Yates on the remaining unplayed songs. Repeat toggles a flag that resets currentIndex on completion.

Recommendations use collaborative filtering: cluster users by listening history embeddings. Find the user's cluster, aggregate top songs not yet heard. Also use content-based filtering: recommend songs with similar audio features (tempo, key, energy) via cosine similarity.

title: Online Code Judge (LeetCode)
description: Design an online code execution and judging platform like LeetCode — users submit code, it runs in a sandbox, and results are evaluated.
functionalRequirements: Problems with description, input/output format, examples, and constraints
Submit code in multiple languages (Python, Java, C++, JavaScript)
Run code against hidden test cases in an isolated sandbox
Judge verdicts: Accepted, Wrong Answer, Time Limit Exceeded, Memory Limit Exceeded, Runtime Error
Show execution time and memory usage for each submission
Global and per-problem leaderboard
Discussion forum per problem
nonFunctionalRequirements: Code execution isolated — cannot affect other submissions or the host
Execution timeout enforced within 10ms of the configured limit
Support 10,000 concurrent submissions
Results returned within 5 seconds for most problems
hints: Core entities: Problem, TestCase, Submission, Judge, ExecutionResult, Leaderboard, User. Submission is placed on a queue. A pool of Judge workers picks submissions, runs them in isolated containers (Docker/WASM), and writes results back.

For sandboxing, spawn a Docker container (or use seccomp-filtered processes) with resource limits: CPU time, memory cap, no network, no filesystem writes outside /tmp. Kill the container after the time limit.

Judge workflow: 1) Compile code (if compiled language); 2) Run against each test case; 3) Compare output with expected (exact or trimmed match); 4) Record verdict for each test; 5) Overall verdict = worst case. Store results in the Submission record.

title: Notification Service
description: Design a multi-channel notification service that sends alerts via push, email, SMS, and in-app with user preference control.
functionalRequirements: Send notifications through multiple channels: push, email, SMS, in-app
Users configure channel preferences per notification type
Notification types: transactional, promotional, alert
Template-based messages with dynamic variable substitution
Delivery tracking: sent, delivered, read, failed
Retry failed notifications with exponential backoff
Scheduled notifications (send at a future time)
Rate limiting to prevent spamming users
nonFunctionalRequirements: Transactional notifications delivered within 5 seconds
Support 1 million notifications per hour
At-least-once delivery with deduplication
hints: Core entities: Notification, NotificationType, Channel (Email/SMS/Push/InApp), Template, UserPreference, DeliveryRecord. Use the Strategy pattern for channels — each Channel implements send(notification) with its own third-party SDK.

Use a Message Queue (Kafka or SQS) as the backbone: when a notification event fires, publish to the queue. Channel-specific consumers pick up messages and deliver via their respective APIs (SendGrid, Twilio, FCM).

Template engine: store templates with placeholders like {{user_name}}, {{order_id}}. On notification creation, merge the template with the event payload. Use the Factory pattern to select the right template per (notificationType, channel) combination.

title: Coupon & Discount System
description: Design a flexible coupon and discount management system for an e-commerce platform supporting various promotion types.
functionalRequirements: Create coupon codes with type: percentage off, flat amount off, free shipping, buy-X-get-Y
Set validity period, minimum order value, and usage limits (total and per-user)
Apply single or multiple coupons to a cart
Auto-apply the best available coupon based on cart contents
Coupon stacking rules: which types can be combined
Admin dashboard to create, disable, and view coupon analytics
Track coupon redemptions per user
nonFunctionalRequirements: Coupon validation under 50ms
Prevent concurrent over-redemption using atomic decrement
Support 100,000 active coupon codes
hints: Core entities: Coupon, DiscountType, UsageLimit, CouponRedemption, Cart, CartItem. Use the Strategy pattern for discount calculation — each DiscountType implements calculate(cart) → discountAmount.

For usage limits, store a redemption counter in Redis with an atomic DECR operation. Before applying: DECR coupon:{code}:remaining. If result < 0, INCR back and reject. This prevents race conditions under high load.

For stacking rules, model a DiscountChain: list of applicable strategies ordered by priority. Use the Chain of Responsibility — each strategy can decide to stop the chain or pass to the next. A StackingRule object defines which coupon types are mutually exclusive.

title: Inventory Management System
description: Design a warehouse inventory system that tracks products, stock levels, restocking, and multi-warehouse fulfillment.
functionalRequirements: Track product stock levels across multiple warehouses
Reserve inventory when an order is placed, release on cancel
Restock items: receive purchase orders from suppliers
Low-stock alerts when quantity drops below threshold
Transfer stock between warehouses
FIFO or LIFO inventory costing for accounting
Barcode/SKU-based product identification
Audit log of all stock movements
nonFunctionalRequirements: Stock reservation is atomic — prevent overselling
Audit log is append-only and immutable
Support 1 million SKUs across 500 warehouses
hints: Core entities: Product, SKU, Warehouse, InventoryItem (product × warehouse), StockReservation, PurchaseOrder, StockMovement, LowStockAlert. InventoryItem tracks quantityOnHand, quantityReserved, quantityAvailable = onHand − reserved.

For atomic reservation, use a database transaction: UPDATE inventory SET reserved = reserved + qty WHERE product_id = ? AND (on_hand - reserved) >= qty. If 0 rows updated, stock is insufficient — roll back and reject.

Model all stock changes as immutable StockMovement records (type: Receive, Reserve, Release, Ship, Transfer, Adjust). The current stock level is the sum of all movements, making auditing trivial and rollback possible.

title: Video Conferencing (Zoom)
description: Design a video conferencing system like Zoom supporting scheduled meetings, screen sharing, recording, and participant management.
functionalRequirements: Schedule meetings with a unique join link and meeting ID
Join meetings as host or participant (up to 100 participants)
Audio and video toggles per participant
Screen and application sharing
In-meeting chat with the group or privately
Recording meetings to cloud or local storage
Waiting room: host admits participants manually
Raise hand and reaction emojis
nonFunctionalRequirements: Audio/video latency < 150ms end-to-end
Support 1,000 concurrent meetings on the platform
Recording stored durably with < 5 second delay
hints: Core entities: User, Meeting, MeetingParticipant, ChatMessage, Recording, WaitingRoom. Meeting has a unique ID and password. Participants join via a Signaling Server that exchanges SDP/ICE candidates for WebRTC peer-to-peer (or SFU-based) connection setup.

For scalability with > 10 participants, use an SFU (Selective Forwarding Unit): each participant sends their stream to the SFU once; the SFU distributes it to all others, reducing each sender's upload burden from O(n) to O(1).

Recording: capture streams at the server level (SFU can forward to a Recording Service). Recording Service muxes audio/video streams per participant into a single MP4 using a container like FFmpeg, then uploads to object storage.

title: Pastebin / Code Snippet Sharing
description: Design a text/code snippet sharing service like Pastebin — create, share, and expire pastes with syntax highlighting.
functionalRequirements: Create a paste with title, content, language, and optional expiry
Generate a unique short URL for each paste
Syntax highlighting for 50+ programming languages
Public, unlisted, and private visibility settings
View, fork, and delete pastes
User accounts to manage their own pastes
Search public pastes by title or content
nonFunctionalRequirements: 10 million pastes created per day
Paste read latency < 50ms via CDN caching
Auto-delete expired pastes with a background job
Content storage scales to petabytes cheaply
hints: Core entities: Paste, User, Language, Visibility. Short URL generation: base62-encode a counter from a distributed ID generator (Snowflake). Store metadata (title, userId, expiry, language) in a relational DB; store large paste content in object storage (S3/GCS) keyed by pasteId.

For read performance, cache paste metadata in Redis (TTL = min(paste expiry, 1 hour)). Serve content from a CDN for public pastes. For private pastes, stream content directly from object storage after auth check.

Expiry: store expiry timestamp in the DB. A background cron job (every 5 min) runs DELETE FROM pastes WHERE expiry < NOW(). Also add a lazy expiry check on reads: if paste is expired, return 410 Gone and trigger async deletion.

title: Cricket Scoreboard / Live Scoring
description: Design a live cricket scoring system supporting match setup, ball-by-ball scoring, innings management, and score broadcasting.
functionalRequirements: Set up a match: teams, players, venue, format (Test, ODI, T20)
Ball-by-ball scoring: runs, wickets, extras (wide, no-ball, bye)
Track batting and bowling statistics per player
Manage innings transitions and follow-on rules
Calculate run rate, required rate, and projected score
Live score broadcast to subscribed clients
Scorecard display: fall of wickets, partnerships, over summary
nonFunctionalRequirements: Score updates broadcast to millions of viewers in < 2 seconds
Ball-by-ball history immutable and append-only
Support 50 concurrent live matches
hints: Core entities: Match, Team, Player, Inning, Over, Ball, BattingCard, BowlingCard, Extras. Match is a State Machine: Toss → FirstInning → InningBreak → SecondInning → Result. Each Ball records runs, wicket info, extras type, and bowler/batsman.

BattingCard and BowlingCard are computed views derived from Ball records — never store them directly. On each ball event, recalculate the active batsman's and bowler's running totals. This makes the history immutable and stats always consistent.

For live broadcast, use the Observer pattern: Match is the subject. When a Ball is added, notify all MatchObservers (WebSocket broadcaster, stats calculator, alert service). The broadcaster pushes the delta (just the new ball) to all subscribed clients rather than the full scorecard.
